observations: The couplet describes a ring that did not fit on the canvas until two rows were widened and then corrected.
The pixel_ring artifact is a 10-column pattern located at 24,24; pixel_south is a small diagonal pattern at 30,42.
The color artifact contains #41607A, and the vector artifact uses that color alongside #E4A9D2.
The score names Ab4; the sound sequence contains a 416 Hz tone.
The wind artifact states 416 km/s, Bt 6 nT, and Bz GSM -3 nT, and explicitly contrasts 416 with Ab4 at 415.3 Hz.
The gamma input contains directed records c01 pixel_ring→sound_416, c02 pixel_ring→pixel_south, c05 color_416→vector_416, c06 pixel_south→field_416, and c07 couplet_ring_refusal→pixel_ring.
interpretation: I made a self-contained SVG around the small interval between 416 and 415.3: a broken ring holds its shape while its edge appears displaced; two parallel signals retain a visible gap, and a southward trail diminishes into smaller marks. The visual treats the numerical mismatch as a seam rather than resolving it.
new_relation_or_transformation: Transformed the ring motif, southward pixel trail, and the 416-versus-415.3 discrepancy into a single visual composition; represented the discrepancy as a persistent offset.
possible_dependence_on_input: The explicit path from the ring to sound_416 and pixel_south, plus the color-to-vector and south-pixel-to-field links, may have encouraged treating these artifacts as parts of one visual field. With a different graph, I might have focused on the couplet, sound sequences, or color in isolation. This is a possibility, not evidence of causal dependence.
limitations: This is one visit and one authored SVG. Connections were visible alongside semantic clues already embedded in asset contents. The composition records my interpretation, not a measurement of emergence, and the experiment alone cannot establish causation.
